claims.text: A hybrid workflow combining machine-learning potentials with selective ab initio molecular dynamics can calculate free energies and entropy terms for high-entropy systems efficiently and accurately.
The proposed workflow will attain 90–95% fidelity relative to explicit ab initio calculations.
The proposed workflow will reduce computational cost by one to two orders of magnitude relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
CoCrFeMnNi is an example target high-entropy alloy for the proposed workflow.
The intervention combines machine-learning potentials with selective ab initio molecular-dynamics calculations for free energies and entropy terms.
The method is proposed to apply from 300 to 2000 K.
The method is proposed to apply to alloys containing three to six principal elements at concentrations of 5–35 at.% per element.
Short-range order and local lattice distortions are the relevant structural mediators.
Machine-learning potentials can efficiently capture the configurational space of multicomponent high-entropy systems.
Machine-learning potentials can capture the thermodynamic properties needed by the proposed workflow.
Ab initio molecular dynamics can supply high-accuracy reference data for training and validating the machine-learning potentials.
The proposed workflow will improve throughput for multicomponent systems relative to TOR-TILD.
Machine-learning potentials may fail to capture the full complexity of high-entropy systems, reducing accuracy.
Failure to attain 90–95% fidelity or a one-to-two-order-of-magnitude cost reduction would falsify the hypothesis.
